claim: A substantial fraction of the metazoan transcriptome undergoes circadian oscillations in many cells and tissues.
source_text: A substantial fraction of the metazoan transcriptome undergoes circadian oscillations in many cells and tissues.
evidence_reasoning: This statement draws from established scientific consensus in the circadian biology field.

claim: Many rhythmic mRNAs manifest poor transcriptional rhythms, indicating a prominent contribution of post-transcriptional regulation to circadian mRNA expression.
source_text: Although many genes are rhythmically transcribed, many rhythmic mRNAs manifest poor transcriptional rhythms, indicating a prominent contribution of post-transcriptional regulation to circadian mRNA expression.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the Nascent-Seq experimental data presented in the manuscript and inferred from the comparison between transcriptional and mRNA rhythms.

claim: The rhythmic DNA binding profile of CLOCK and BMAL1 does not determine the transcriptional phase of most target genes.
source_text: This analysis of rhythmic transcription also showed that the rhythmic DNA binding profile of the transcription factors CLOCK and BMAL1 does not determine the transcriptional phase of most target genes.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by ChIP-Seq and Nascent-Seq experimental data comparing CLK:BMAL1 binding phases with transcriptional phases.

claim: CLK:BMAL1 likely collaborates with other transcription factors in a gene-specific manner.
source_text: This likely reflects gene-specific collaborations of CLK:BMAL1 with other transcription factors.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the heterogeneous transcriptional phases observed despite uniform CLK:BMAL1 binding phases, supported by experimental data.

claim: The circadian system in eukaryotes is based on cell-autonomous molecular oscillators which rely on transcriptional feedback loops.
source_text: The circadian system in eukaryotes is based on cell-autonomous molecular oscillators, which rely on transcriptional feedback loops.
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge in the field, as indicated by the review citations (Ko and Takahashi, 2006; Dardente and Cermakian, 2007).

claim: BMAL1 acts as a dimer with either CLOCK or NPAS2 to activate transcription of many genes in mammals.
source_text: In mammals, the transcription factor BMAL1 acts as a dimer with either CLOCK (CLK) or Neuronal PAS domain protein 2 (NPAS2) to activate the transcription of many genes, including the transcriptional repressors Period (Per1, Per2 and Per3) and Cryptochrome (Cry1 and Cry2).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the mammalian circadian clock mechanism, supported by review citations.

claim: Up to 10-15% of all mRNAs in a single mammalian tissue exhibit rhythmic expression.
source_text: up to 10–15% of all mRNAs in a single mammalian tissue; Lowrey and Takahashi, 2004; Vollmers et al., 2009
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Lowrey and Takahashi, 2004; Vollmers et al., 2009).

claim: Post-transcriptional regulation contributes to rhythmic mRNA expression of several genes, including core clock genes.
source_text: There are, however, a few reports indicating that post-transcriptional regulation contributes to rhythmic mRNA expression of several genes, including core clock genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to review articles (Kojima et al., 2011; Staiger and Green, 2011; Staiger and Koster, 2011; Zhang et al., 2011).

claim: Post-transcriptional events rhythmically regulate the mRNA half-life of Per2, Cry1, and per genes.
source_text: For example, post-transcriptional events rhythmically regulate the mRNA half-life of the mammalian clock genes Per2 and Cry1 and the Drosophila clock gene per (So and Rosbash, 1997; Woo et al., 2009; Woo et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by specific citations to studies demonstrating post-transcriptional regulation of these genes.

claim: Approximately 15% of all detected genes in mouse liver are rhythmically transcribed.
source_text: Although many genes are rhythmically transcribed in the mouse liver (∼15% of all detected genes)
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by the Nascent-Seq experimental data from this study.

claim: Only 42% of rhythmically transcribed genes show mRNA oscillations.
source_text: only 42% of these rhythmically transcribed genes show mRNA oscillations
evidence_reasoning: This is directly calculated from the comparison of Nascent-Seq and RNA-Seq datasets in this study.

claim: About 70% of genes that exhibit rhythmic mRNA expression do not show transcriptional rhythms.
source_text: about 70% of the genes that exhibit rhythmic mRNA expression do not show transcriptional rhythms, suggesting that post-transcriptional regulation plays a major role in defining the rhythmic mRNA landscape
evidence_reasoning: This is directly calculated from the experimental data and used to infer the importance of post-transcriptional regulation.

claim: Approximately 65-70% of Nascent-Seq sequences uniquely mapped to the mouse genome.
source_text: Removal of rRNA was unnecessary as approximately 65–70% of the sequences uniquely mapped to the genome
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct measurement from the sequencing data analysis.

claim: Seventy-six percent of uniquely mapped Nascent-Seq sequences map to introns.
source_text: Seventy six percent of these uniquely mapped sequences map to introns
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct measurement from the sequencing data analysis showing the distribution of reads.

claim: Nascent-Seq signal exhibits a 5' to 3' gradient.
source_text: Nascent-Seq signal exhibits increased intron signal and a 5ʹ to 3ʹ gradient signal (arrow).
evidence_reasoning: This is observed directly in the visualization of Nascent-Seq data.

claim: Genes with high Nascent-Seq/RNA-Seq ratios have relatively short mRNA half-lives.
source_text: genes with a high ratio have relatively short half-lives, and genes with low ratios have longer mRNA half-lives
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by correlation analysis between Nascent-Seq/RNA-Seq ratios and published mRNA half-life data.

claim: Genes with high Nascent-Seq/RNA-Seq ratios are enriched for non-coding RNA, G-coupled protein receptors, regulation of transcription and chromatin organization.
source_text: Genes with a high ratio (top 10% of all genes) are dramatically enriched for specific functions, namely, non-coding RNA (ncRNA), G-coupled protein receptors, regulation of transcription and chromatin organization
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by gene ontology analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Genes with low Nascent-Seq/RNA-Seq ratios are enriched for genes involved in ribosome function and mitochondrial respiration.
source_text: Genes with a low ratio are enriched for genes involved in ribosome function and mitochondrial respiration
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by gene ontology analysis of the experimental data.

claim: mRNA stability contributes to the wide range of Nascent-Seq to RNA-Seq ratios.
source_text: These data indicates that mRNA stability contributes to the wide range of Nascent-Seq to RNA-Seq ratios.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the correlation between Nascent-Seq/RNA-Seq ratios and mRNA half-lives.

claim: 963 genes are rhythmically transcribed in mouse liver.
source_text: Heatmap representation of Nascent-Seq signal for the 963 genes that are rhythmically transcribed in the mouse liver.
evidence_reasoning: This is the result of statistical analysis of the Nascent-Seq dataset using defined criteria for rhythmicity.

claim: Fewer genes are transcribed at ZT16-20.
source_text: Analysis of their distribution reveals that fewer genes are transcribed at ZT16-20.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed from the phase distribution analysis of rhythmically transcribed genes.

claim: Rhythmic Nascent-Seq signal was detected for many precursors of non-coding RNAs such as pri-miRNA and long non-coding RNA.
source_text: Rhythmic Nascent-Seq signal was detected for many precursors of non-coding RNAs such as pri-miRNA (d, pri-miR122a) and long non-coding RNA(e, lin-ncRNAs BC019819, AK157581, BC049268, BC056646).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the Nascent-Seq data for specific ncRNA genes.

claim: The fraction of rhythmic mRNA (22.1%) was higher than the fraction of rhythmic nascent RNA (15.1%).
source_text: the fraction of rhythmic mRNA was higher than the fraction of rhythmic nascent RNA (22.1% and 15.1%, respectively
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from statistical analysis of both RNA-Seq and Nascent-Seq datasets.

claim: Only 41.6% of rhythmically transcribed genes also manifest rhythmic mRNA expression.
source_text: only 41.6% of rhythmically transcribed genes also manifest rhythmic mRNA expression (R-R gene set; 342/822
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the comparison of rhythmic genes in Nascent-Seq and RNA-Seq datasets.

claim: The phases of rhythmic nascent RNA and mRNA expression are highly correlated (r = 0.92) for genes with both rhythmic transcription and mRNA.
source_text: Both phases are highly correlated (r = 0.92).
evidence_reasoning: This correlation coefficient is calculated from the phase data of R-R genes.

claim: The amplitudes of mRNA expression rhythms are correlated with nascent RNA expression rhythms (r = 0.76).
source_text: Amplitude of mRNA expression rhythms are correlated with nascent RNA expression rhythms (r = 0.76).
evidence_reasoning: This correlation coefficient is calculated from amplitude measurements of R-R genes.

claim: 58.4% of rhythmically transcribed genes do not show robust mRNA expression.
source_text: The other 58.4% of rhythmically transcribed genes (480/822) do not show robust mRNA expression (R-AR gene set
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the comparison of rhythmic genes in Nascent-Seq and RNA-Seq datasets.

claim: Only 28.4% of genes with rhythmic mRNA expression have rhythmic transcription that meets the cycling criteria.
source_text: The opposite comparison is based on genes with rhythmic mRNA expression, of which only 28.4% (342/1204) have rhythmic transcription that meets the cycling criteria
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the comparison of rhythmic genes in RNA-Seq and Nascent-Seq datasets.

claim: Most cycling mRNAs (862/1204) likely undergo post-transcriptional regulation.
source_text: indicates that most cycling mRNAs (862/1204) likely undergo post-transcriptional regulation
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that these genes have rhythmic mRNA but arrhythmic transcription.

claim: 25 of the 480 R-AR genes' Nascent-Seq rhythms can be attributed to the rhythmic transcription of an adjacent gene.
source_text: Nascent-Seq rhythms of 25 of the 480 R-AR genes can be attributed to the rhythmic transcription of an adjacent gene.
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by manual inspection of the Nascent-Seq data showing read-through transcription.

claim: The standard deviation of nascent RNA expression is higher than the standard deviation of mRNA levels for most AR-R genes.
source_text: Standard deviation (SD; calculated using the 12 time points and normalized to the mean) of nascent RNA expression is higher than the SD normalized to the mean of mRNA levels for most AR-R genes.
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the variability analysis of the 12 time points for AR-R genes.

claim: Higher transcriptional variability of arrhythmically transcribed genes is associated with higher occurrence of rhythmic mRNA expression.
source_text: Higher transcriptional variability (SD) of arrhythmically transcribed genes is associated with higher occurrence of rhythmic mRNA expression
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by correlation analysis between transcriptional variability and rhythmic mRNA expression.

claim: Higher variability of transcription is associated with increased amplitude of rhythms at both nascent RNA and mRNA levels.
source_text: Higher variability of transcription for the genes of the AR-R group is associated with increase amplitude of rhythms at both Nascent RNA (brown) and mRNA (red) level.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by binning AR-R genes by variability and comparing rhythm amplitudes.

claim: 10% of the AR-R gene set (86/862) exhibit high transcription at only one time point.
source_text: Manual inspection of AR-R genes with high variability revealed a set of genes with high transcription at only one time point (10% of the AR-R gene set; 86/862).
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by manual inspection of the data for AR-R genes with high variability.

claim: A higher number of predicted miRNA target sites was found for AR-R genes with low transcriptional variability compared to genes with higher transcriptional variability.
source_text: Indeed, a higher number of predicted miRNA target sites was found for these genes compared to genes with higher transcriptional variability (using MirTarget2; p<0.01)
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by computational analysis of predicted miRNA target sites.

claim: AR-R genes with highly variable transcription were enriched for responsive genes and metabolic genes.
source_text: AR-R genes with highly variable transcription were enriched for responsive genes (GO: response to stimulus) and metabolic genes
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by gene ontology analysis of AR-R genes with high transcriptional variability.

claim: CLK and BMAL1 target many DNA binding sites in mouse liver (759 and 1579, respectively).
source_text: CLK and BMAL1 target many DNA binding sites in mouse liver (759 and 1579, respectively)
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by ChIP-Seq analysis using the MACS algorithm.

claim: CLK and BMAL1 significantly overlap on 211 DNA binding peaks.
source_text: significantly overlap on 211 of these peaks
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by computational analysis of overlapping ChIP-Seq peaks.

claim: CLK and BMAL1 binding sites are enriched for the canonical consensus sequence CACGTG.
source_text: they are enriched for the canonical consensus sequence CACGTG
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by motif analysis of the ChIP-Seq peaks.

claim: 184 direct target genes are identified by the 211 CLK:BMAL1 DNA binding sites.
source_text: almost all of the 184 direct target genes identified by the 211 CLK:BMAL1 DNA binding sites
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by computational assignment of ChIP-Seq peaks to genes.

claim: CLK:BMAL1 targets include 12 ncRNA genes, including a cluster of four rhythmically transcribed ncRNAs.
source_text: There are for example 12 ncRNA genes, which include a cluster of four rhythmically transcribed ncRNAs
evidence_reasoning: This is identified from the list of CLK:BMAL1 target genes and their annotation.

claim: CLK:BMAL1 target genes are significantly enriched for rhythmically transcribed genes.
source_text: CLK:BMAL1 target genes are significantly enriched for rhythmically transcribed genes (chi-square test, p<0.0001
evidence_reasoning: This is determined by statistical analysis comparing the proportion of rhythmic genes among CLK:BMAL1 targets vs all genes.

claim: Only 50% of CLK:BMAL1 target genes are rhythmically transcribed.
source_text: only 50% of CLK:BMAL1 target genes are rhythmically transcribed
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the Nascent-Seq data for CLK:BMAL1 target genes.

claim: The peak transcriptional phases of CLK:BMAL1 target genes are heterogeneous and distributed throughout the day.
source_text: the peak transcriptional phases of CLK:BMAL1 target genes are heterogeneous and distributed throughout the day
evidence_reasoning: This is observed from phase distribution analysis of rhythmically transcribed CLK:BMAL1 target genes.

claim: The levels of Per1, Per2 and Cry1 pre-mRNAs in Bmal1−/− mice are higher than the trough of expression in wild-type mice.
source_text: The levels of Per1, Per2 and Cry1 pre-mRNAs in Bmal1−/− mice are higher than the trough of expression in wild-type mice, indicating that other transcriptional regulators are indeed important for the transcription of these three clock genes
evidence_reasoning: This is measured by qPCR and used to infer the involvement of other transcriptional regulators.

claim: Per2 has a prominent anti-sense transcript at times of low Per2 sense transcription.
source_text: Per2 has a prominent anti-sense transcript at times of low Per2 sense transcription
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the strand-specific Nascent-Seq data for Per2.

claim: Antisense transcription could be an additional mechanism responsible for the disconnect between the phase of CLK:BMAL1 DNA binding and the phase of rhythmic transcription.
source_text: This suggests that antisense transcription could be an additional mechanism responsible for the disconnect between the phase of CLK:BMAL1 DNA binding and the phase of rhythmic transcription.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculated based on the observation of antisense transcription at Per2, but not definitively proven.

claim: Post-transcriptional events buffer variable transcriptional output to generate robust and reproducible rhythms of mRNA expression.
source_text: This suggests that post-transcriptional events buffer variable transcriptional output to generate robust and reproducible rhythms of mRNA expression
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that variable transcription in AR-R genes correlates with rhythmic mRNA expression.

claim: The half-lives of nascent transcripts are generally much shorter than those of mRNA.
source_text: Because the half-lives of nascent transcripts are generally much shorter than those of mRNA (Griffiths-Jones, 2007; Mattick, 2009; Mercer et al., 2009; Wang and Chang, 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous studies on RNA half-lives.

claim: A short burst of transcription can result in elevated mRNA expression that lasts several hours.
source_text: a short burst of transcription can result in elevated mRNA expression that lasts several hours, as has been shown in systems involving an acute inflammatory response (Cheadle et al., 2005; Hao and Baltimore, 2009)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to studies in other biological systems.

claim: Generic mRNA stability cannot account for the buffering of transcriptional variability, as many genes with arrhythmic but variable transcription do not exhibit rhythmic mRNA expression.
source_text: However, generic mRNA stability cannot account for this buffering, as many genes with arrhythmic but variable transcription do not exhibit rhythmic mRNA expression
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that not all genes with variable transcription show rhythmic mRNA.

claim: The post-transcriptional buffering is clock-controlled and selective for specific genes.
source_text: This suggests that the post-transcriptional buffering is clock-controlled and selective for specific genes.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the selective nature of which genes with variable transcription show rhythmic mRNA.

claim: Transcriptional output is not identical for all CLK:BMAL1 target genes.
source_text: This indicates that transcriptional output is not identical for all target genes
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the heterogeneous transcriptional phases of CLK:BMAL1 target genes.

claim: CLK:BMAL1 cooperates with other transcription factors to establish the phase of transcription.
source_text: suggests that CLK:BMAL1 cooperates with other transcription factors to establish the phase of transcription, as previously shown only for the Cry1 gene (Ukai-Tadenuma et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the heterogeneous phases and supported by a citation showing this for Cry1.

claim: Transcription of most CLK:BMAL1 target genes is arrhythmic but not absent without BMAL1.
source_text: In addition, transcription of most of these target genes is arrhythmic but not absent without BMAL1.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by qPCR measurements in Bmal1−/− mice.

claim: Core CLK:CYC target genes in flies exhibit a discrete phase of expression that matches the phase of DNA binding.
source_text: This feature of target gene expression as well as the heterogeneity of phase is unlike what is observed in flies: core CLK:CYC target genes exhibit a discrete phase of expression that matches the phase of DNA binding (Abruzzi et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to a previous study on Drosophila circadian regulation.

claim: Nascent RNA was extracted from purified nuclei using high salt/urea/detergent buffer.
source_text: To this end, nascent RNA was extracted from purified nuclei using the high salt/urea/detergent buffer originally described by Wuarin and Schibler (1994).
evidence_reasoning: This describes the methodology used, citing the original protocol.

claim: A similar sequencing strategy was recently applied to macrophage nascent RNA by Smale, Black and colleagues.
source_text: A very similar sequencing strategy was recently applied by Smale, Black and colleagues to macrophage nascent RNA (Bhatt et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This cites a similar application of the technique in another system.

claim: Nascent-Seq signal extends past the annotated 3' end of genes.
source_text: Nascent-Seq signal (brown), but not RNA-Seq signal (red), extends past the annotated 3ʹend of the genes B4galt1 and Nfx1.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the visualization of Nascent-Seq data.

claim: Less than 5% of genes with a read per base pair superior to three exhibit a 1.3-fold gene signal variation between technical replicates.
source_text: Less than 5% of the genes with a read per base pair superior to three exhibit a 1.3-fold gene signal variation.
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the technical replicate analysis to determine the threshold for reliable gene expression measurements.
